title: Preservation and triangulation for native compactly supported Weil image
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the categories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(-)$ and the actual equivariant derived operations $h^*,Rh_*,Rh_{0!}$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $h:V\to W$ be a separated quasi-compact locally finite-type morphism of $k_0$-schemes, with $W$ quasi-compact, quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and locally of finite type over $k_0$. Then the ambient construction $Rh_{0!}$ carries bounded objects with constructible cohomology to bounded objects with constructible cohomology. The full categories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)$ and $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W)$ with their inherited shifts and distinguished triangles are triangulated, and the restricted functor
$$Rh_{0!}:\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)\longrightarrow\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W)$$
is triangulated: it has its derived shift comparison $Rh_{0!}(L[1])\cong (Rh_{0!}L)[1]$ and sends distinguished triangles, including the last arrow through this comparison, to distinguished triangles.

source.place: WeilComplex.objectProperty_rightDerivedLowerShriek, lines 115-142; CommShift and IsTriangulated instances, lines 201-217; WeilSheaf/Category.lean lines 217-247 for the inherited triangulation. All proofs are present in the project source; this is not a finite-coefficient Mathlib specialization.

proof.text: The structure morphism of $W$ is finite type, since it is locally of finite type and quasi-compact. Finite-type composition makes $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ finite type. Apply Nagata to the separated finite-type map $h$ and the quasi-compact quasi-separated target $W$: $h$ is compactifiable. Take the compactification used in the native framework, $V\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}W$; by the definition of compactification used there, $j$ is an open immersion, $p$ is proper and $pj=h$. Give $Z$ its $k_0$-structure through $p$. Properness includes finite type, so finite-type composition makes $Z$ finite type over $k_0$. Both legs are over $k_0$, since $pj=h$. The chosen compactification is not required to have a quasi-compact first leg, so this is checked: $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is Noetherian, hence $Z$, of finite type over it, is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma. Every open subset of the Noetherian space $|Z|$ is quasi-compact, and $j$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset, so the inverse image under $j$ of every open of $Z$ is quasi-compact: $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. In particular the locally finite-type and quasi-compactness assumptions needed below hold for $V,Z,W$ and $j$; no absolute separatedness of these schemes is inferred.

proof.text: Use the current framework's coefficient sheaf on the whole underlying topological space and its constructibility condition, whose finite rank may depend on each pro-etale covering member. For each $T=V,Z,W$, let $\mathcal C_T\subset\mathcal W_T$ consist of the constructible native Weil sheaves. The native abelian lemma supplies a Grothendieck abelian ambient category and exactly the zero, isomorphism, kernel, cokernel and extension closure hypotheses on $\mathcal C_T$. The weak-Serre cohomology lemma, including its bounded intersection clause, therefore gives the inherited triangulated structure on $D^b_{\mathcal C_T}(\mathcal W_T)=\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T)$. The equality here is the definition in the framework. Grothendieck K-injective existence gives K-injective resolutions in each ambient category, so the total right derived functors used below have the hypotheses required by the unbounded triangulated right-derived-functor lemma.

source.place: objectProperty_rightDerivedLowerShriek and ambient/restricted CommShift and IsTriangulated instances, lines 115-217; proof expanded through native heart finiteness and bounded truncations

proof.text: Let $K\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)$ and put $J=D(j_{0!})K$, the termwise functor induced on derived categories by the exact functor $j_{0!}$ (exact-functor derived-triangulation lemma). The native open-extension lemma makes $j_{0!}$ exact and constructible-preserving. The exact-functor cohomology comparison applied to a complex representing $K$ gives $H^n(J)\cong j_{0!}H^n(K)$. Because an additive exact functor sends zero to zero, every cohomological interval for $K$ is also an interval for $J$. Each displayed cohomology sheaf is constructible by the same native lemma. Thus $J\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(Z)$. This calculation takes place in the derived categories of the equivariant abelian categories.

source.place: objectProperty_rightDerivedLowerShriek and ambient/restricted CommShift and IsTriangulated instances, lines 115-217; proof expanded through native heart finiteness and bounded truncations

proof.text: Write $P=Rp_{0*}$. The proper-heart finiteness lemma supplies the additive left-exact functor $p_{0*}$. Apply the unbounded right-derived-functor lemma, using the K-injectives from step 2: $P$ commutes with integer shifts and is triangulated on the ambient categories. Define $Q(M)$ to mean that $P(M)$ belongs to $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W)$. This property contains zero, is invariant under isomorphism and is closed under extensions in distinguished triangles, by triangulation of $P$ and step 2. Choose a finite interval containing the cohomology of $J$. For every integer $q$ and every $M\in\mathcal C_Z$, proper-heart finiteness applied to $M$ gives $P(M[0])\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W)$; the shift comparison of $P$ and shift closure of that category give $Q(M[0][-q])$. This is the devissage hypothesis; by step 3 each $H^q(J)$ lies in $\mathcal C_Z$. Apply bounded degreewise truncation devissage with $P_q=\mathcal C_Z$ to conclude $Q(J)$. Its hypotheses hold also for an empty interval, when $J$ is zero. Hence $Rp_{0*}D(j_{0!})K=Rh_{0!}K$ is bounded with constructible cohomology.

source.place: objectProperty_rightDerivedLowerShriek and ambient/restricted CommShift and IsTriangulated instances, lines 115-217; proof expanded through native heart finiteness and bounded truncations

proof.text: The exact-functor derived-triangulation lemma makes $D(j_{0!})$ triangulated on the ambient derived categories. Together with the preceding triangulation of $P$, this makes $F=P\circ D(j_{0!})$ triangulated: apply the first functor and then the second to a distinguished triangle. Its shift comparison is the composite $F(L[1])\to P(D(j_{0!})L[1])\to F(L)[1]$, first applying $P$ to the exact termwise shift comparison and then using the derived shift comparison of $P$. The last arrow of the resulting triangle is precisely the image of the original last arrow followed by this composite. The native framework defines the ambient $Rh_{0!}$ as this very composite.

source.place: objectProperty_rightDerivedLowerShriek and ambient/restricted CommShift and IsTriangulated instances, lines 115-217; proof expanded through native heart finiteness and bounded truncations

proof.text: Step 4 shows that $F$ restricts to the two full bounded constructible categories from step 2. Its shift comparisons have source and target in the target full subcategory, so they are isomorphisms there with the same inverses. A distinguished triangle in the source is an ambient distinguished triangle with its vertices in the source full subcategory. Step 5 sends it, with the stated last arrow, to an ambient distinguished triangle; step 4 puts all three vertices in the target full subcategory. By the inherited definition this is a distinguished triangle there. Thus the restricted $Rh_{0!}$ has exactly the claimed shift comparison and triangulated-functor property.
